HubSpot vs Zoho vs Pipedrive: CRM Compared

These three CRMs win at three different jobs: HubSpot for an all-in-one platform, Zoho for value and customization, and Pipedrive for pure sales focus. This compares them by the decision that actually matters — which one fits how your team works, with an honest note on who each is wrong for.

By The GridDojo Team Published August 28, 2026 5 min read

HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Pipedrive turn up on almost every shortlist of the best CRM for a small business — and it is easy to stall comparing their feature lists, because on paper they overlap heavily. The more useful question is not which has the most features, but which one is built for the way your team actually works. Each of these three is designed around a different idea of what a CRM is for, and that is what should decide it. Here is how they compare on the things that matter, with a clear pick for each situation and an honest note on who should look elsewhere.

The one-line difference

  • HubSpot is an all-in-one platform — sales, marketing, and support in one place, with the most generous free tier.
  • Zoho CRM is the value and customization pick — a lot of capability for a low price, if you invest time to set it up.
  • Pipedrive is the pure sales tool — the simplest, fastest way to run a deal pipeline, with no free plan.

Descriptions here are based on each vendor's current documented plans, not on hands-on testing. Pricing and plan limits change often, so treat any detail as "at the time of writing" and confirm it on each vendor's own pricing page before you commit.

Best for an all-in-one platform: HubSpot

HubSpot's pitch is breadth: contacts, deals, email marketing, forms, and customer support all live on one platform, and its free CRM is the most generous of the three — enough for a small team to run without paying. That unification is the real advantage. If you want your sales pipeline, your marketing emails, and your support tickets sharing the same contact records, HubSpot does that out of the box while the others lean on add-ons or separate apps.

Best for: growing teams that want sales, marketing, and service unified, and a strong free starting point. Skip it if: you only need a sales pipeline — you would be adopting a broad platform (and its higher-tier pricing as you grow) for a fraction of what it does.

Best for value and customization: Zoho CRM

Zoho CRM consistently offers the most capability per dollar, especially once you move past entry tiers, and it is deeply customizable — fields, modules, workflows, and automation you can shape to your process. It also has a free plan for a small team and plugs into the wider Zoho ecosystem of business apps. The cost of that flexibility is time: Zoho rewards teams willing to configure it, and it can feel like a lot at first.

Best for: budget-conscious teams that want depth and are happy to set the tool up to fit their process. Skip it if: you want to be productive in an afternoon with zero configuration — Zoho's flexibility has a learning curve.

Best for pure sales focus: Pipedrive

Pipedrive does one thing and does it cleanly: it runs a visual sales pipeline that salespeople find intuitive from day one. It is widely regarded as the easiest of the three to set up and use daily, because it is not trying to also be a marketing or support platform. The trade-off is scope — there is no permanent free plan, only a trial, and marketing and service features are minimal by design.

Best for: teams that are 100% focused on sales and value fast onboarding and a frictionless pipeline. Skip it if: you need a free plan, or you want marketing and support living in the same tool.

How to decide

  • Want one platform for sales, marketing, and support — and a free start → HubSpot.
  • Want the most capability for the money and will invest setup time → Zoho CRM.
  • Run a sales-only team and want the simplest daily pipeline → Pipedrive.
  • Not sure yet → start with a free tier of HubSpot or Zoho; both let you import a spreadsheet and try before you pay.
Tip: This is a shortlist of three, not the whole field. For the wider set of options and how to weigh them, see the best CRM for small businesses, and if free is your priority, the best free CRM covers where each free tier's limits bite.

Whichever you lean toward, run the same short test before committing: put real contacts and one real deal through its free tier or trial for a week. Frequently asked questions

Which is better, HubSpot, Zoho, or Pipedrive?

None is best overall — they win at different jobs. HubSpot suits teams wanting an all-in-one platform with a generous free tier, Zoho suits budget-conscious teams that want customization, and Pipedrive suits sales-only teams that want the simplest pipeline. Match the tool to how your team works.

Which of the three has the best free plan?

HubSpot has the most generous free CRM, and Zoho offers a free plan for a small team. Pipedrive has no permanent free plan — only a trial — so if a free tier is essential, HubSpot or Zoho are the realistic choices.

Is Pipedrive better than HubSpot for a small business?

It depends on your needs. Pipedrive is better if you are purely sales-focused and want the fastest, simplest pipeline. HubSpot is better if you want sales, marketing, and support in one platform and a free starting point. Neither is universally better.

Can I switch between these CRMs later?

Yes, though switching is disruptive, so it is worth choosing carefully. All three import contacts and deals from a CSV file, so you can move your data in — and, if needed, export it out — but you will have to rebuild pipelines, automations, and integrations in the new tool.
